# My AI Infrastructure Stack

**28 Services, 6 Zones, 1 Self-Improving System**

After months of building, breaking, and rebuilding, my AI infrastructure has settled into a stable architecture that handles everything from content publishing to autonomous self-improvement. This post documents the full stack — not as a how-to, but as a snapshot of what's actually running in production right now.

---

## The Big Picture

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,">

The stack is organised into six zones, each responsible for a distinct capability. Everything runs in Docker on a single Ubuntu server, connected via internal Docker networking with selective port exposure.

---

## Zone 1: AI Agent Layer

The brain of the operation. Every interaction flows through **OpenCode** — a CLI-based AI agent that has access to 60+ specialised skills, a question tool for structured decision-making, and a consultation mode (Brain) for deep reasoning.

The key design principle: **the agent is sovereign**. It decides which tools to use, when to ask for help, and when to escalate. The Question Tool is critical — instead of guessing what the user wants, the agent presents structured options with recommendations.

> [!NOTE]
> OpenCode runs as a CLI tool, not a container. It accesses all other services via their exposed ports on `localhost`. This means it can use any service in the stack without additional networking configuration.

**Skills are the modular units of capability.** Each skill is a markdown file with structured metadata, trigger words, and progressive disclosure layers (L0 minimal → L4 full reference). The skill system is itself managed by a Meta-Factory that creates, validates, and evolves skills autonomously.

---

## Zone 2: CMS and Content

Content flows through **Directus** as the single source of truth. Blog posts, pages, and metadata all live in Directus and are consumed by multiple frontends.

The publishing pipeline:

🔴 `Write(Markdown)` → 🟠 `Push(Directus API)` → 🟡 `Build(Astro)` → 🟢 `Publish(Static)` → ✅ `Live`

| Component | Port | Role |
|-----------|------|------|
| Directus CMS | 8055 | API-first headless CMS, single source of truth |
| Astro Blog | 3002 | Static site generator, fetches from Directus at build time |
| NextExplorer | 8080 | Web-based file browser/editor for Docker volumes |
| FreshRSS | 8088 | RSS aggregator for the attention pipeline |
| Memos | 5230 | Quick notes and decisions feeding the memory system |

The Astro blog uses a custom markdown pipeline with multiple extensions:

- **Shiki** for syntax highlighting (dual light/dark themes)
- **Callouts** for NOTE, TIP, WARNING, DANGER boxes
- **Tabs** for tabbed code sections
- **Toggles** for collapsible content panels
- **Shortcodes** for quizzes, timelines, comparisons
- **TOC sidebar** with scroll highlighting
- **Scroll reveal** animations via Intersection Observer

> [!TIP]
> Content is stored in Directus, not as files. The blog fetches from the API at build time. This means every build gets the latest content without file syncing.

---

## Zone 3: RAG and Knowledge

This is where retrieval-augmented generation lives. Three knowledge stores, each serving a different purpose:

| Store | Technology | Purpose | Size |
|-------|-----------|---------|------|
| OpenRAG | OpenSearch + pgvector | Document retrieval for research queries | 2,800+ documents |
| pgvector Memory | PostgreSQL + pgvector | Persistent AI memories with embeddings | 1,348+ memories |
| Neo4j Graph | Neo4j | Entity relationships for graph-enriched retrieval | Research knowledge graphs |

**LiteLLM** acts as a unified model gateway, routing requests to different LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, local models) through a single API. This enables cost-aware model routing — cheaper models for routine tasks, frontier models for complex reasoning.

---

## Zone 4: Libraries and Frameworks

The foundational layers that everything else builds on.

| Library | Role | Why |
|---------|------|-----|
| **Pydantic** | Data validation | Every schema, config, and API request is validated with Pydantic models |
| **OpenCode SDK** | Agent framework | The skill system, trigger words, progressive disclosure — all built on this |
| **PostgreSQL** | Primary database | Directus, pgvector memory, OpenRAG, and more — all backed by PostgreSQL |
| **Docker** | Container runtime | Every service runs in Docker with compose for orchestration |

> [!TIP]
> PostgreSQL is the backbone. We run 4 separate PostgreSQL instances: Directus CMS, pgvector memory, OpenRAG knowledge base, and supermarket scraper data. Each has its own container and volume, but they all share the same engine.

---

## Zone 5: Observability

The monitoring stack follows the OpenTelemetry standard, with data flowing through a collector to multiple backends.

| Component | Purpose | Status |
|-----------|---------|--------|
| **OTEL Collector** | Receives telemetry from all services (gRPC :4317, HTTP :4318) | Active |
| **Prometheus** | Scrapes metrics from Node Exporter, OTEL, Docker daemon | Active |
| **Grafana** | Dashboards for system overview, AI performance, container health (port 3003) | Active |
| **Jaeger** | Distributed tracing for request flow analysis | Active |

Key dashboards:
- **System overview** — CPU, memory, disk, network across all containers
- **AI agent performance** — task completion rates, iterations, cost per session
- **Container health** — restarts, resource limits, volume usage

**Kestra** is planned but not yet deployed. It will handle workflow orchestration — scheduling recurring tasks like the attention pipeline, memory cleanup, and automated blog publishing. Currently these run via cron jobs.

---

## Zone 6: MCP and Integration

MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers extend the agent's capabilities by providing additional tools at runtime.

| MCP Server | Purpose | Status |
|------------|---------|--------|
| **Context7** | Fetch up-to-date library documentation | Active |
| **Playwright** | Browser automation and testing | Active |
| **Agent Browser** | Full browser control with snapshots | Active |
| **GitHub MCP** | Repository integration (issues, PRs, code) | Active |
| **Brave Search** | Web search for research | Active |

The MCP architecture means the agent's toolset is **extensible at runtime**. Adding a new capability is as simple as configuring an MCP server — no code changes required.

> [!WARNING]
> More MCP servers = larger context window consumption. Each active server adds to the prompt size. I keep only the servers I actively use enabled and disable the rest.

---

## How It All Connects

The data flows between zones:

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,">

The data flow diagram shows how services connect:

- **OpenCode** uses MCP tools, publishes to Directus, and accesses LiteLLM
- **Directus CMS** feeds content to the Astro Blog
- **OpenRAG** queries OpenSearch and uses pgvector for embeddings
- **pgvector** enriches knowledge through Neo4j graph relationships
- All services emit telemetry to the OTEL Collector, feeding Prometheus and Grafana

The architecture is designed for **modularity and replaceability**. Any component can be swapped out without touching the others. PostgreSQL can become CockroachDB. OpenSearch can become Pinecone. Grafana can become Datadog. The interfaces are standard; the implementations are interchangeable.
